---
title: "OLS mathematics and Rust notes"
---

Follow the [executed OLS walkthrough](notebooks/ols-math.qmd) for intermediate
matrices and calculations, and the [three-way verification](verifications/ols.qmd)
for equivalent fits in R, statsmodels and PHP. Missing-data deletion happens in
the binding before estimation; all formulas below use the retained sample.

## Least squares

For an $n \times p$ design matrix $X$ and outcome vector $y$, choose

$$
\hat\beta=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\beta}(y-X\beta)^\top(y-X\beta).
$$

Differentiating the quadratic gives gradient $-2X^\top(y-X\beta)$. Setting it
to zero produces the normal equations:

$$
X^\top X\hat\beta=X^\top y.
$$

This characterizes the answer, but computing the inverse of $X^\top X$ squares
the condition number and can lose accuracy. In `crates/stats-core/src/ols.rs`,
we scale columns with a diagonal matrix $D$ and decompose
$A=XD^{-1}=USV^\top$. The least-squares solution is
$\hat\beta=D^{-1}VS^{-1}U^\top y$. nalgebra's SVD `solve` performs this
calculation. Singular values at numerical zero indicate a rank failure. Scaling
makes the rank decision less dependent on predictor units.

The numerical engine uses nalgebra's Rust-native decomposition, with no
external BLAS or LAPACK dependency.

Fitted values are $X\hat\beta$, residuals are $y-X\hat\beta$, and
$\mathrm{RSS}$ is the squared residual norm. Full rank uses $p$ estimated
coefficients and leaves $n-p$ residual degrees of freedom. The unbiased estimate
of error variance is $s^2=\mathrm{RSS}/(n-p)$. The conventional covariance is

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\beta)
=s^2(X^\top X)^{-1}
=s^2D^{-1}VS^{-2}V^\top D^{-1}.
$$

The code computes the final expression directly from the SVD. Standard errors
are square roots of its diagonal. Under Gaussian independent errors,
$(\hat\beta_j-\beta_j)/\mathrm{SE}_j$ has a Student $t$ distribution with
$n-p$ degrees of freedom. For the null $\beta_j=0$, the reported statistic is
$\hat\beta_j/\mathrm{SE}_j$. Two-sided p-values use twice the upper tail at
its absolute value. Confidence limits are
$\hat\beta_j\pm t_{0.975,n-p}\,\mathrm{SE}_j$. The survival function
preserves precision for small p-values.

With an explicit ones column, $\mathrm{TSS}=\sum_i(y_i-\bar y)^2$;
otherwise $\mathrm{TSS}=\sum_i y_i^2$. We report
$R^2=1-\mathrm{RSS}/\mathrm{TSS}$. Adjusted $R^2$ is
$1-(1-R^2)(n-1)/(n-p)$ with an intercept, or
$1-(1-R^2)n/(n-p)$ without one. See the
[contracts](contracts.qmd) for zero-variance and perfect-fit conventions.

## Gaussian likelihood

Assume independent observations

$$
y_i\sim N(x_i^\top\beta,\sigma^2).
$$

Multiplying their densities and taking logs turns the product into a sum:

$$
\ell(\beta,\sigma^2)
=-\frac n2\log(2\pi\sigma^2)
-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_i(y_i-x_i^\top\beta)^2.
$$

For any positive fixed variance, maximizing this expression with respect to
$\beta$ minimizes $\mathrm{RSS}$, giving the OLS coefficients.
Differentiating with respect to the variance gives
$-n/(2\sigma^2)+\mathrm{RSS}/(2\sigma^4)=0$, so the ML estimate is
$\mathrm{RSS}/n$. Substitution yields

$$
\ell(\hat\beta,\hat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{ML}})
=-\frac n2\left[\log(2\pi)+\log(\mathrm{RSS}/n)+1\right].
$$

This is the likelihood returned by the code. ML variance differs from
$\mathrm{RSS}/(n-p)$: estimating coefficients consumes $p$ degrees of freedom,
so dividing by $n-p$ corrects the downward bias for inference. At
$\mathrm{RSS}=0$, the positive-variance model has no finite maximum:
likelihood grows without bound as variance approaches zero. The code reports
positive infinity as the limiting log-likelihood.

## Rust constructs in this implementation

`fit_ols` takes ownership of `Vec<Vec<f64>>` and `Vec<f64>`: it can consume them
with `into_iter()` without copying. Validation uses borrowed iterators (`iter()`)
to inspect values before moving them. The binding borrows PHP's `ZendHashTable`
for the duration of the call, copying numeric values into Rust-owned vectors.

`OlsResult` is a struct grouping named outputs. `StatsError` holds a readable
message and implements Display and Error. `Result<OlsResult, StatsError>` forces
the caller to handle failure. The `?` operator returns early on an error; the PHP
binding uses `map_err` to convert it into a `PhpException`. No PHP types appear
in stats-core.

Vectors own variable-length data. Borrowed slices and iterators let us inspect
that data without taking ownership. `map`, `collect`, `any` and `sum` express the
coefficient, validation and scalar calculations. `Vec<[f64; 2]>` stores each
confidence interval as a fixed-size pair.

nalgebra's `DMatrix` and `DVector` have runtime dimensions and own their storage.
`from_row_iterator` accepts the flattened row-wise design; nalgebra stores its
matrix column-wise internally. Indexing `(i,j)` accesses a row and column.
Borrowing `&design` and `&beta` during multiplication keeps them available for
later calculations. SVD consumes the scaled matrix, and its singular values and
right singular vectors provide both the fit and covariance.

In `crates/php-extension/src/lib.rs`, `#[php_function]` exports functions and
`#[php_module]` registers them. Input values are inspected explicitly so strings
and booleans cannot silently become numbers. The binding filters null/NAN rows
listwise, reports original positions and warns on successful omission; strict
mode rejects missingness. Rust still receives complete finite vectors. `ZendHashTable::insert` and the
crate's `IntoZval` conversions turn Rust floats, vectors and nested vectors into
PHP values. The owned `ZBox<ZendHashTable>` uses PHP-managed allocation. The
binding has no statistical calculations beyond selecting the result fields.
